   691→// addCheckpointTrailer adds the Entire-Checkpoint trailer to a commit message.
   692→// Handles proper trailer formatting (blank line before trailers if needed).
   693→func addCheckpointTrailer(message string, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) string {
   694→	trailer := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ": " + checkpointID.String()
   695→
   696→	// If message already ends with trailers (lines starting with key:), just append
   697→	// Otherwise, add a blank line first
   698→	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(message, "\n"), "\n")
   699→
   700→	// Check if last non-empty, non-comment line looks like a trailer
   701→	// Git comment lines start with # and may contain ": " (e.g., "# Changes to be committed:")
   702→	hasTrailers := false
   703→	for i := len(lines) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
   704→		line := strings.TrimSpace(lines[i])
   705→		if line == "" {
   706→			break
   707→		}
   708→		// Skip git comment lines
   709→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
   710→			continue
   711→		}
   712→		if strings.Contains(line, ": ") {
   713→			hasTrailers = true
   714→			break
   715→		}
   716→		// Non-comment, non-trailer line found - no existing trailers
   717→		break
   718→	}
   719→
   720→	if hasTrailers {
   721→		// Append trailer directly
   722→		return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n" + trailer + "\n"
   723→	}
   724→
   725→	// Add blank line before trailer
   726→	return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n"
   727→}
   728→
   729→// addCheckpointTrailerWithComment adds the Entire-Checkpoint trailer with an explanatory comment.
   730→// The trailer is placed above the git comment block but below the user's message area,
   731→// with a comment explaining that the user can remove it if they don't want to link the commit
   732→// to the agent session. If prompt is non-empty, it's shown as context.
   733→func addCheckpointTrailerWithComment(message string, checkpointID id.CheckpointID, agentName, prompt string) string {
   734→	trailer := trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ": " + checkpointID.String()
   735→	commentLines := []string{
   736→		"# Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above if you don't want to link this commit to " + agentName + " session context.",
   737→	}
   738→	if prompt != "" {
   739→		commentLines = append(commentLines, "# Last Prompt: "+prompt)
   740→	}
   741→	commentLines = append(commentLines, "# The trailer will be added to your next commit based on this branch.")
   742→	comment := strings.Join(commentLines, "\n")
   743→
   744→	lines := strings.Split(message, "\n")
   745→
   746→	// Find where the git comment block starts (first # line)
   747→	commentStart := -1
   748→	for i, line := range lines {
   749→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "#") {
   750→			commentStart = i
   751→			break
   752→		}
   753→	}
   754→
   755→	if commentStart == -1 {
   756→		// No git comments, append trailer at the end
   757→		return strings.TrimRight(message, "\n") + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n"
   758→	}
   759→
   760→	// Split into user content and git comments
   761→	userContent := strings.Join(lines[:commentStart], "\n")
   762→	gitComments := strings.Join(lines[commentStart:], "\n")
   763→
   764→	// Build result: user content, blank line, trailer, comment, blank line, git comments
   765→	userContent = strings.TrimRight(userContent, "\n")
   766→	if userContent == "" {
   767→		// No user content yet - leave space for them to type, then trailer
   768→		// Two newlines: first for user's message line, second for blank separator
   769→		return "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n\n" + gitComments
   770→	}
   771→	return userContent + "\n\n" + trailer + "\n" + comment + "\n\n" + gitComments
   772→}
   773→
   774→// InitializeSession creates session state for a new session or updates an existing one.
   775→// This implements the optional SessionInitializer interface.
   776→// Called during UserPromptSubmit to allow git hooks to detect active sessions.
   777→//
   778→// If the session already exists and HEAD has moved (e.g., user committed), updates
   779→// BaseCommit to the new HEAD so future checkpoints go to the correct shadow branch.
   780→//
   781→// If there's an existing shadow branch with commits from a different session ID,
   782→// returns a SessionIDConflictError to prevent orphaning existing session work.
   783→//
   784→// agentType is the human-readable name of the agent (e.g., "Claude Code").
   785→// transcriptPath is the path to the live transcript file (for mid-session commit detection).
   786→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) InitializeSession(sessionID string, agentType agent.AgentType, transcriptPath string) error {
   787→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   788→	if err != nil {
   789→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open git repository: %w", err)
   790→	}
   791→
   792→	// Check if session already exists
   793→	state, err := s.loadSessionState(sessionID)
   794→	if err != nil {
   795→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to check session state: %w", err)
   796→	}
   797→
   798→	if state != nil && state.BaseCommit != "" {
   799→		// Session is fully initialized
   800→		needSave := false
   801→
   802→		// Backfill AgentType if empty (for sessions created before the agent_type field was added)
   803→		if state.AgentType == "" && agentType != "" {
   804→			state.AgentType = agentType
   805→			needSave = true
   806→		}
   807→
   808→		// Update transcript path if provided (may change on session resume)
   809→		if transcriptPath != "" && state.TranscriptPath != transcriptPath {
   810→			state.TranscriptPath = transcriptPath
   811→			needSave = true
   812→		}
   813→
   814→		// Clear LastCheckpointID on every new prompt
   815→		// This is set during PostCommit when a checkpoint is created, and should be
   816→		// cleared when the user enters a new prompt (starting fresh work)
   817→		if state.LastCheckpointID != "" {
   818→			state.LastCheckpointID = ""
   819→			needSave = true
   820→		}
   821→
   822→		// Calculate attribution at prompt start (BEFORE agent makes any changes)
   823→		// This captures user edits since the last checkpoint (or base commit for first prompt).
   824→		// IMPORTANT: Always calculate attribution, even for the first checkpoint, to capture
   825→		// user edits made before the first prompt. The inner CalculatePromptAttribution handles
   826→		// nil lastCheckpointTree by falling back to baseTree.
   827→		promptAttr := s.calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(repo, state)
   828→		state.PendingPromptAttribution = &promptAttr
   829→		needSave = true
   830→
   831→		// Check if HEAD has moved (user pulled/rebased or committed)
   832→		// migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded handles renaming the shadow branch and updating state.BaseCommit
   833→		migrated, err := s.migrateShadowBranchIfNeeded(repo, state)
   834→		if err != nil {
   835→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to check/migrate shadow branch: %w", err)
   836→		}
   837→		if migrated {
   838→			needSave = true
   839→		}
   840→
   841→		if needSave {
   842→			if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   843→				return fmt.Errorf("failed to update session state: %w", err)
   844→			}
   845→		}
   846→		return nil
   847→	}
   848→	// If state exists but BaseCommit is empty, it's a partial state from concurrent warning
   849→	// Continue below to properly initialize it
   850→
   851→	// Initialize new session
   852→	state, err = s.initializeSession(repo, sessionID, agentType, transcriptPath)
   853→	if err != nil {
   854→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize session: %w", err)
   855→	}
   856→
   857→	// Calculate attribution for pre-prompt edits
   858→	// This captures any user edits made before the first prompt
   859→	promptAttr := s.calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(repo, state)
   860→	state.PendingPromptAttribution = &promptAttr
   861→	if err = s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   862→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save attribution: %w", err)
   863→	}
   864→
   865→	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Initialized shadow session: %s\n", sessionID)
   866→	return nil
   867→}
   868→
   869→// calculatePromptAttributionAtStart calculates attribution at prompt start (before agent runs).
   870→// This captures user changes since the last checkpoint - no filtering needed since
   871→// the agent hasn't made any changes yet.
   872→//
   873→// IMPORTANT: This reads from the worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
   874→// captures in checkpoints. If we read staged content but checkpoints capture worktree content,
   875→// unstaged changes would be in the checkpoint but not counted in PromptAttribution, causing
   876→// them to be incorrectly attributed to the agent later.
   877→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(
   878→	repo *git.Repository,
   879→	state *SessionState,
   880→) PromptAttribution {
   881→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "attribution")
   882→	nextCheckpointNum := state.StepCount + 1
   883→	result := PromptAttribution{CheckpointNumber: nextCheckpointNum}
   884→
   885→	// Get last checkpoint tree from shadow branch (if it exists)
   886→	// For the first checkpoint, no shadow branch exists yet - this is fine,
   887→	// CalculatePromptAttribution will use baseTree as the reference instead.
   888→	var lastCheckpointTree *object.Tree
   889→	shadowBranchName := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   890→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   891→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   892→	if err != nil {
   893→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: no shadow branch yet (first checkpoint)",
   894→			slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName))
   895→		// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
   896→	} else {
   897→		shadowCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   898→		if err != nil {
   899→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow commit",
   900→				slog.String("shadow_ref", ref.Hash().String()),
   901→				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   902→			// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
   903→		} else {
   904→			lastCheckpointTree, err = shadowCommit.Tree()
   905→			if err != nil {
   906→				logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow tree",
   907→					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   908→				// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
   909→			}
   910→		}
   911→	}
   912→
   913→	// Get base tree for agent lines calculation
   914→	var baseTree *object.Tree
   915→	if baseCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(state.BaseCommit)); err == nil {
   916→		if tree, treeErr := baseCommit.Tree(); treeErr == nil {
   917→			baseTree = tree
   918→		} else {
   919→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: base tree unavailable",
   920→				slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()))
   921→		}
   922→	} else {
   923→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: base commit unavailable",
   924→			slog.String("base_commit", state.BaseCommit),
   925→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   926→	}
   927→
   928→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
   929→	if err != nil {
   930→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution skipped: failed to get worktree",
   931→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   932→		return result
   933→	}
   934→
   935→	// Get worktree status to find ALL changed files
   936→	status, err := worktree.Status()
   937→	if err != nil {
   938→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution skipped: failed to get worktree status",
   939→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   940→		return result
   941→	}
   942→
   943→	worktreeRoot := worktree.Filesystem.Root()
   944→
   945→	// Build map of changed files with their worktree content
   946→	// IMPORTANT: We read from worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
   947→	// captures in checkpoints. This ensures attribution is consistent.
   948→	changedFiles := make(map[string]string)
   949→	for filePath, fileStatus := range status {
   950→		// Skip unmodified files
   951→		if fileStatus.Worktree == git.Unmodified && fileStatus.Staging == git.Unmodified {
   952→			continue
   953→		}
   954→		// Skip .entire metadata directory (session data, not user code)
   955→		if strings.HasPrefix(filePath, paths.EntireMetadataDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(filePath, ".entire/") {
   956→			continue
   957→		}
   958→
   959→		// Always read from worktree to match checkpoint behavior
   960→		fullPath := filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, filePath)
   961→		var content string
   962→		if data, err := os.ReadFile(fullPath); err == nil { //nolint:gosec // filePath is from git worktree status
   963→			// Use git's binary detection algorithm (matches getFileContent behavior).
   964→			// Binary files are excluded from line-based attribution calculations.
   965→			isBinary, binErr := binary.IsBinary(bytes.NewReader(data))
   966→			if binErr == nil && !isBinary {
   967→				content = string(data)
   968→			}
   969→		}
   970→		// else: file deleted, unreadable, or binary - content remains empty string
   971→
   972→		changedFiles[filePath] = content
   973→	}
   974→
   975→	// Use CalculatePromptAttribution from manual_commit_attribution.go
   976→	result = CalculatePromptAttribution(baseTree, lastCheckpointTree, changedFiles, nextCheckpointNum)
   977→
   978→	return result
   979→}

   981→// getStagedFiles returns a list of files staged for commit.
   982→func getStagedFiles(repo *git.Repository) []string {
   983→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
   984→	if err != nil {
   985→		return nil
   986→	}
   987→
   988→	status, err := worktree.Status()
   989→	if err != nil {
   990→		return nil
   991→	}
   992→
   993→	var staged []string
   994→	for path, fileStatus := range status {
   995→		// Check if file is staged (in index)
   996→		if fileStatus.Staging != git.Unmodified && fileStatus.Staging != git.Untracked {
   997→			staged = append(staged, path)
   998→		}
   999→	}
  1000→	return staged
  1001→}

  1003→// getLastPrompt retrieves the most recent user prompt from a session's shadow branch.
  1004→// Returns empty string if no prompt can be retrieved.
  1005→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) getLastPrompt(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) string {
  1006→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
  1007→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
  1008→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
  1009→	if err != nil {
  1010→		return ""
  1011→	}
  1012→
  1013→	// Extract session data to get prompts for commit message generation
  1014→	// Pass agent type to handle different transcript formats (JSONL for Claude, JSON for Gemini)
  1015→	sessionData, err := s.extractSessionData(repo, ref.Hash(), state.SessionID, nil, state.AgentType)
  1016→	if err != nil || len(sessionData.Prompts) == 0 {
  1017→		return ""
  1018→	}
  1019→
  1020→	// Return the last prompt (most recent work before commit)
  1021→	return sessionData.Prompts[len(sessionData.Prompts)-1]
  1022→}

  1024→// hasOverlappingFiles checks if any file in stagedFiles appears in filesTouched.
  1025→func hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, filesTouched []string) bool {
  1026→	touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
  1027→	for _, f := range filesTouched {
  1028→		touchedSet[f] = true
  1029→	}
  1030→
  1031→	for _, staged := range stagedFiles {
  1032→		if touchedSet[staged] {
  1033→			return true
  1034→		}
  1035→	}
  1036→	return false
  1037→}

   109→// PromptAttribution captures line-level attribution data at the start of each prompt.
   110→// By recording what changed since the last checkpoint BEFORE the agent works,
   111→// we can accurately separate user edits from agent contributions.
   112→type PromptAttribution struct {
   113→	// CheckpointNumber is which checkpoint this was recorded before (1-indexed)
   114→	CheckpointNumber int `json:"checkpoint_number"`
   115→
   116→	// UserLinesAdded is lines added by user since the last checkpoint
   117→	UserLinesAdded int `json:"user_lines_added"`
   118→
   119→	// UserLinesRemoved is lines removed by user since the last checkpoint
   120→	UserLinesRemoved int `json:"user_lines_removed"`
   121→
   122→	// AgentLinesAdded is total agent lines added so far (base → last checkpoint).
   123→	// Always 0 for checkpoint 1 since there's no previous checkpoint to measure against.
   124→	AgentLinesAdded int `json:"agent_lines_added"`
   125→
   126→	// AgentLinesRemoved is total agent lines removed so far (base → last checkpoint).
   127→	// Always 0 for checkpoint 1 since there's no previous checkpoint to measure against.
   128→	AgentLinesRemoved int `json:"agent_lines_removed"`

   136→// NormalizeAfterLoad applies backward-compatible migrations to state loaded from disk.
   137→// Call this after deserializing a State from JSON.
   138→func (s *State) NormalizeAfterLoad() {
   139→	// Migrate transcript fields: CheckpointTranscriptStart replaces both
   140→	// CondensedTranscriptLines and TranscriptLinesAtStart from older state files.
   141→	if s.CheckpointTranscriptStart == 0 {
   142→		if s.CondensedTranscriptLines > 0 {
   143→			s.CheckpointTranscriptStart = s.CondensedTranscriptLines
   144→		} else if s.TranscriptLinesAtStart > 0 {
   145→			s.CheckpointTranscriptStart = s.TranscriptLinesAtStart
   146→		}
   147→	}
   148→	// Clear deprecated fields so they aren't re-persisted
   149→	s.CondensedTranscriptLines = 0
   150→	s.TranscriptLinesAtStart = 0
   151→}

   212→// Save saves the session state atomically.
   213→func (s *StateStore) Save(ctx context.Context, state *State) error {
   214→	_ = ctx // Reserved for future use
   215→
   216→	// Validate session ID to prevent path traversal
   217→	if err := validation.ValidateSessionID(state.SessionID); err != nil {
   218→		return fmt.Errorf("invalid session ID: %w", err)
   219→	}

   221→	if err := os.MkdirAll(s.stateDir, 0o750); err != nil {
   222→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session state directory: %w", err)
   223→	}

   226→	if err != nil {
   227→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session state: %w", err)
   228→	}
   229→
   230→	stateFile := s.stateFilePath(state.SessionID)

   233→	tmpFile := stateFile + ".tmp"
   234→	if err := os.WriteFile(tmpFile, data, 0o600); err != nil {
   235→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session state: %w", err)
   236→	}
   237→	if err := os.Rename(tmpFile, stateFile); err != nil {
   238→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to rename session state file: %w", err)
   239→	}
   240→	return nil
   241→}

   281→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state directory: %w", err)
   282→	}
   283→
   284→	var states []*State
   285→	for _, entry := range entries {
   286→		if entry.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".json") {
   287→			continue
   288→		}
   289→		if strings.HasSuffix(entry.Name(), ".tmp") {

   313→// In a regular checkout, this is .git/
   314→// In a worktree, this is the main repo's .git/ (not .git/worktrees/<name>/)
   315→func getGitCommonDir() (string, error) {
   316→	ctx := context.Background()
   317→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir")
   318→	cmd.Dir = "."
   319→	output, err := cmd.Output()
   320→	if err != nil {

   322→	}

   328→	if !filepath.IsAbs(commonDir) {

   297→// mergeFilesTouched merges multiple file lists into existing touched files, deduplicating.
   298→func mergeFilesTouched(existing []string, fileLists ...[]string) []string {

   301→		seen[f] = true
   302→	}
   303→
   304→	for _, list := range fileLists {
   305→		for _, f := range list {
   306→			seen[f] = true
   307→		}
   308→	}
   309→
   310→	result := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
   311→	for f := range seen {
   312→		result = append(result, f)
   313→	}
   314→
   315→	// Sort for deterministic output
   316→	sort.Strings(result)
   317→	return result
   318→}

   320→// accumulateTokenUsage adds new token usage to existing accumulated usage.
   321→// If existing is nil, returns a copy of incoming. If incoming is nil, returns existing unchanged.
   322→func accumulateTokenUsage(existing, incoming *agent.TokenUsage) *agent.TokenUsage {
   323→	if incoming == nil {
   324→		return existing
   325→	}
   326→	if existing == nil {
   327→		// Return a copy to avoid sharing the pointer
   328→		return &agent.TokenUsage{
   329→			InputTokens:         incoming.InputTokens,
   330→			CacheCreationTokens: incoming.CacheCreationTokens,
   331→			CacheReadTokens:     incoming.CacheReadTokens,
   332→			OutputTokens:        incoming.OutputTokens,
   333→			APICallCount:        incoming.APICallCount,
   334→			SubagentTokens:      incoming.SubagentTokens,
   335→		}
   336→	}
   337→
   338→	// Accumulate values
   339→	existing.InputTokens += incoming.InputTokens
   340→	existing.CacheCreationTokens += incoming.CacheCreationTokens
   341→	existing.CacheReadTokens += incoming.CacheReadTokens
   342→	existing.OutputTokens += incoming.OutputTokens
   343→	existing.APICallCount += incoming.APICallCount
   344→
   345→	// Accumulate subagent tokens if present
   346→	if incoming.SubagentTokens != nil {
   347→		existing.SubagentTokens = accumulateTokenUsage(existing.SubagentTokens, incoming.SubagentTokens)
   348→	}
   349→
   350→	return existing
   351→}

    41→// ExtractToolUseIDFromTaskMetadataDir extracts the ToolUseID from a task metadata directory path.
    42→// Task metadata dirs have format: .entire/metadata/<session>/tasks/<toolUseID>
    43→// Returns empty string if not a task metadata directory.
    44→func ExtractToolUseIDFromTaskMetadataDir(metadataDir string) string {
    45→	parts := strings.Split(metadataDir, "/")
    46→	if len(parts) >= 2 && parts[len(parts)-2] == "tasks" {
    47→		return parts[len(parts)-1]
    48→	}
    49→	return ""
    50→}

   142→// SaveContext contains all information needed for saving changes.

   163→	// MetadataDirAbs is the absolute path to the session metadata directory

   172→	// AuthorName is the name to use for commits

   183→	StepTranscriptStart      int    // Transcript line count when this step/turn started

   189→// TaskCheckpointContext contains all information needed for saving a task checkpoint.
   190→// This is called by the PostToolUse[Task] hook when a subagent completes.
   191→// The strategy is responsible for creating metadata structures and storing them
   192→// according to its storage approach.
   193→type TaskCheckpointContext struct {
   194→	// SessionID is the Claude Code session identifier
   195→	SessionID string
   196→
   197→	// ToolUseID is the unique identifier for this Task tool invocation
   198→	ToolUseID string
   199→
   200→	// AgentID is the subagent identifier (from tool_response.agentId)
   201→	AgentID string
   202→
   203→	// ModifiedFiles is the list of files modified by the subagent
   204→	// (extracted from the subagent's transcript)

   206→
   207→	// NewFiles is the list of new files created by the subagent
   208→	// (computed from pre-task state comparison)
   209→	NewFiles []string
   210→
   211→	// DeletedFiles is the list of files deleted by the subagent
   212→	DeletedFiles []string
   213→
   214→	// TranscriptPath is the path to the main session transcript
   215→	TranscriptPath string
   216→
   217→	// SubagentTranscriptPath is the path to the subagent's transcript (if available)
   218→	SubagentTranscriptPath string
   219→
   220→	// CheckpointUUID is the UUID for transcript truncation when rewinding
   221→	CheckpointUUID string
   222→
   223→	// AuthorName is the name to use for commits
   224→	AuthorName string
   225→
   226→	// AuthorEmail is the email to use for commits
   227→	AuthorEmail string
   228→
   229→	// IsIncremental indicates this is an incremental checkpoint during task execution,
   230→	// not a final task completion checkpoint. When true:
   231→	// - Writes to checkpoints/NNN-{tool-use-id}.json instead of checkpoint.json
   232→	// - Skips transcript handling
   233→	// - Uses incremental commit message
   234→	IsIncremental bool
   235→
   236→	// IncrementalSequence is the checkpoint sequence number (1, 2, 3, ...)
   237→	// Only used when IsIncremental is true
   238→	IncrementalSequence int
   239→
   240→	// IncrementalType is the tool that triggered this checkpoint ("TodoWrite", "Edit", etc.)
   241→	// Only used when IsIncremental is true
   242→	IncrementalType string
   243→
   244→	// IncrementalData is the tool_input payload for this checkpoint
   245→	// Only used when IsIncremental is true
   246→	IncrementalData json.RawMessage
   247→
   248→	// SubagentType is the type of subagent (e.g., "dev", "reviewer")
   249→	// Extracted from tool_input.subagent_type in Task tool
   250→	// Used for descriptive commit messages
   251→	SubagentType string
   252→
   253→	// TaskDescription is the task description provided to the subagent
   254→	// Extracted from tool_input.description in Task tool
   255→	// Used for descriptive commit messages

   257→
   258→	// TodoContent is the content of the in-progress todo item

   263→	// AgentType is the human-readable agent name (e.g., "Claude Code", "Cursor")

   267→// TaskCheckpoint contains the checkpoint information written to checkpoint.json
   268→type TaskCheckpoint struct {
   269→	SessionID      string `json:"session_id"`

   274→
   275→// SubagentCheckpoint represents an intermediate checkpoint created during subagent execution.
   276→// These are created by PostToolUse hooks for tools like TodoWrite, Edit, Write.
   277→type SubagentCheckpoint struct {
   278→	Type      string          `json:"type"`        // Tool name: "TodoWrite", "Edit", "Write"
   279→	ToolUseID string          `json:"tool_use_id"` // The tool use ID that created this checkpoint

   284→// TaskMetadataDir returns the path to a task's metadata directory
   285→// within the session metadata directory.
   286→func TaskMetadataDir(sessionMetadataDir, toolUseID string) string {
   287→	return sessionMetadataDir + "/tasks/" + toolUseID
   288→}
   289→
   290→// ReadTaskCheckpoint reads the checkpoint.json file from a task metadata directory.
   291→// This is used during rewind to get the checkpoint UUID for transcript truncation.
   292→func ReadTaskCheckpoint(taskMetadataDir string) (*TaskCheckpoint, error) {
   293→	checkpointFile := taskMetadataDir + "/checkpoint.json"
   294→
   295→	data, err := os.ReadFile(checkpointFile) //nolint:gosec // Reading from controlled git metadata path
   296→	if err != nil {
   297→		return nil, err
   298→	}
   299→
   300→	var checkpoint TaskCheckpoint
   301→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &checkpoint); err != nil {
   302→		return nil, err
   303→	}
   304→
   305→	return &checkpoint, nil
   306→}

   308→// Strategy defines the interface for git operation strategies.
   309→// Different implementations can use commits, branches, stashes, etc.
   310→//
   311→// Note: State capture (tracking untracked files before a session) is handled
   312→// by the CLI layer, not the strategy. The strategy receives pre-computed
   313→// file lists in SaveContext.
   314→type Strategy interface {
   315→	// Name returns the strategy identifier (e.g., "commit", "branch", "stash")
   316→	Name() string
   317→
   318→	// Description returns a human-readable description for the setup wizard
   319→	Description() string
   320→
   321→	// AllowsMainBranch returns true if this strategy can safely operate on the
   322→	// default branch (main/master). Strategies that don't modify the working
   323→	// branch's commit history (like manual-commit strategies) can return true.
   324→	// Strategies that create commits on the working branch should return false
   325→	// to prevent polluting main branch history.
   326→	AllowsMainBranch() bool
   327→
   328→	// ValidateRepository checks if the repository is in a valid state
   329→	// for this strategy to operate. Returns an error if validation fails.
   330→	ValidateRepository() error
   331→
   332→	// SaveChanges is called on Stop to save all session changes
   333→	// using this strategy's approach (commit, branch, stash, etc.)
   334→	SaveChanges(ctx SaveContext) error
   335→
   336→	// SaveTaskCheckpoint is called by PostToolUse[Task] hook when a subagent completes.
   337→	// Creates a checkpoint commit with task metadata for later rewind.
   338→	// Different strategies may handle this differently:
   339→	// - Commit strategy: commits to active branch
   340→	// - Manual-commit strategy: commits to shadow branch
   341→	// - Auto-commit strategy: commits logs to shadow only (code deferred to Stop)
   342→	SaveTaskCheckpoint(ctx TaskCheckpointContext) error
   343→
   344→	// GetRewindPoints returns available points to rewind to.
   345→	// The limit parameter controls the maximum number of points to return.
   346→	GetRewindPoints(limit int) ([]RewindPoint, error)
   347→
   348→	// Rewind restores the repository to the given rewind point.
   349→	// The metadataDir in the point is used to restore the session transcript.
   350→	Rewind(point RewindPoint) error
   351→
   352→	// CanRewind checks if rewinding is currently possible.
   353→	// Returns (canRewind, reason if not, error)
   354→	CanRewind() (bool, string, error)
   355→
   356→	// PreviewRewind returns what will happen if rewinding to the given point.
   357→	// This allows showing warnings about files that will be deleted before the rewind.
   358→	// Returns nil if preview is not supported (e.g., auto-commit strategy).
   359→	PreviewRewind(point RewindPoint) (*RewindPreview, error)
   360→
   361→	// GetTaskCheckpoint returns the task checkpoint for a given rewind point.
   362→	// For strategies that store checkpoints in git (auto-commit), this reads from the branch.
   363→	// For strategies that store checkpoints on disk (commit, manual-commit), this reads from the filesystem.
   364→	// Returns nil, nil if not a task checkpoint or checkpoint not found.
   365→	GetTaskCheckpoint(point RewindPoint) (*TaskCheckpoint, error)
   366→
   367→	// GetTaskCheckpointTranscript returns the session transcript for a task checkpoint.
   368→	// For strategies that store transcripts in git (auto-commit), this reads from the branch.
   369→	// For strategies that store transcripts on disk (commit, manual-commit), this reads from the filesystem.
   370→	GetTaskCheckpointTranscript(point RewindPoint) ([]byte, error)
   371→
   372→	// GetSessionInfo returns session information for linking commits.
   373→	// This is used by the context command to generate trailers.
   374→	// Returns ErrNoSession if no session info is available.
   375→	GetSessionInfo() (*SessionInfo, error)
   376→
   377→	// EnsureSetup ensures the strategy's required setup is in place,
   378→	// installing any missing pieces (git hooks, gitignore entries, etc.).
   379→	// Returns nil if setup is complete or was successfully installed.
   380→	EnsureSetup() error
   381→
   382→	// NOTE: ListSessions and GetSession are standalone functions in session.go.
   383→	// They read from entire/sessions and merge with SessionSource if implemented.
   384→
   385→	// GetMetadataRef returns a reference to the metadata commit for the given checkpoint.
   386→	// Format: "<branch>@<commit-sha>" (e.g., "entire/sessions@abc123").
   387→	// Returns empty string if not applicable (e.g., commit strategy with filesystem metadata).
   388→	GetMetadataRef(checkpoint Checkpoint) string
   389→
   390→	// GetSessionMetadataRef returns a reference to the most recent metadata commit for a session.
   391→	// Format: "<branch>@<commit-sha>" (e.g., "entire/sessions@abc123").
   392→	// Returns empty string if not applicable or session not found.
   393→	GetSessionMetadataRef(sessionID string) string
   394→
   395→	// GetSessionContext returns the context.md content for a session.
   396→	// Returns empty string if not available.
   397→	GetSessionContext(sessionID string) string
   398→
   399→	// GetCheckpointLog returns the session transcript for a specific checkpoint.
   400→	// For strategies that store transcripts in git branches (auto-commit, manual-commit),
   401→	// this reads from the checkpoint's commit tree.
   402→	// For strategies that store on disk (commit), reads from the filesystem.
   403→	// Returns ErrNoMetadata if transcript is not available.
   404→	GetCheckpointLog(checkpoint Checkpoint) ([]byte, error)
   405→}
   406→
   407→// SessionInitializer is an optional interface for strategies that need to
   408→// initialize session state when a user prompt is submitted.
   409→// Strategies like manual-commit use this to create session state files that
   410→// the git prepare-commit-msg hook can detect.
   411→type SessionInitializer interface {
   412→	// InitializeSession creates session state for a new session.
   413→	// Called during UserPromptSubmit hook before any checkpoints are created.
   414→	// agentType is the human-readable name of the agent (e.g., "Claude Code").
   415→	// transcriptPath is the path to the live transcript file (for mid-session commit detection).
   416→	InitializeSession(sessionID string, agentType agent.AgentType, transcriptPath string) error
   417→}
   418→
   419→// PrepareCommitMsgHandler is an optional interface for strategies that need to
   420→// handle the git prepare-commit-msg hook.
   421→type PrepareCommitMsgHandler interface {
   422→	// PrepareCommitMsg is called by the git prepare-commit-msg hook.
   423→	// It can modify the commit message file to add trailers, etc.
   424→	// The source parameter indicates how the commit was initiated:
   425→	//   - "" or "template": normal editor flow
   426→	//   - "message": using -m or -F flag
   427→	//   - "merge": merge commit
   428→	//   - "squash": squash merge
   429→	//   - "commit": amend with -c/-C
   430→	// Should return nil on errors to not block commits (log warnings to stderr).
   431→	PrepareCommitMsg(commitMsgFile string, source string) error
   432→}
   433→
   434→// PostCommitHandler is an optional interface for strategies that need to
   435→// handle the git post-commit hook.
   436→type PostCommitHandler interface {
   437→	// PostCommit is called by the git post-commit hook after a commit is created.
   438→	// Used to perform actions like condensing session data after commits.
   439→	// Should return nil on errors to not block subsequent operations (log warnings to stderr).
   440→	PostCommit() error
   441→}
   442→
   443→// CommitMsgHandler is an optional interface for strategies that need to
   444→// handle the git commit-msg hook.
   445→type CommitMsgHandler interface {
   446→	// CommitMsg is called by the git commit-msg hook after the user edits the message.
   447→	// Used to validate or modify the final commit message before the commit is created.
   448→	// If this returns an error, the commit is aborted.
   449→	CommitMsg(commitMsgFile string) error
   450→}
   451→
   452→// PrePushHandler is an optional interface for strategies that need to
   453→// handle the git pre-push hook.
   454→type PrePushHandler interface {
   455→	// PrePush is called by the git pre-push hook before pushing to a remote.
   456→	// Used to push session branches (e.g., entire/sessions) alongside user pushes.
   457→	// The remote parameter is the name of the remote being pushed to.
   458→	// Should return nil on errors to not block pushes (log warnings to stderr).
   459→	PrePush(remote string) error
   460→}
   461→
   462→// LogsOnlyRestorer is an optional interface for strategies that support
   463→// restoring session logs without file state restoration.
   464→// This is used for "logs-only" rewind points where only the session transcript
   465→// can be restored (file state requires git checkout).
   466→type LogsOnlyRestorer interface {
   467→	// RestoreLogsOnly restores session logs from a logs-only rewind point.
   468→	// Does not modify the working directory - only restores the transcript
   469→	// to Claude's project directory.
   470→	// If force is false, prompts for confirmation when local logs have newer timestamps.
   471→	RestoreLogsOnly(point RewindPoint, force bool) error
   472→}
   473→
   474→// SessionResetter is an optional interface for strategies that support
   475→// resetting session state and shadow branches.
   476→// This is used by the "rewind reset" command to clean up shadow branches
   477→// and session state when a user wants to start fresh.
   478→type SessionResetter interface {
   479→	// Reset deletes the shadow branch and session state for the current HEAD.
   480→	// Returns nil if there's nothing to reset (no shadow branch).
   481→	Reset() error
   482→}
   483→
   484→// ConcurrentSessionChecker is an optional interface for strategies that support
   485→// counting concurrent sessions with uncommitted changes.
   486→// This is used by the SessionStart hook to show an informational message about
   487→// how many other active conversations will be included in the next commit.
   488→type ConcurrentSessionChecker interface {
   489→	// CountOtherActiveSessionsWithCheckpoints returns the number of other active sessions
   490→	// with uncommitted checkpoints on the same base commit.
   491→	// Returns 0, nil if no such sessions exist.
   492→	CountOtherActiveSessionsWithCheckpoints(currentSessionID string) (int, error)
   493→}
   494→
   495→// SessionSource is an optional interface for strategies that provide additional
   496→// sessions beyond those stored on the entire/sessions branch.
   497→// For example, manual-commit strategy provides active sessions from .git/entire-sessions/
   498→// that haven't yet been condensed to entire/sessions.
   499→//
   500→// ListSessions() automatically discovers all registered strategies, checks if they
   501→// implement SessionSource, and merges their additional sessions by ID.
   502→type SessionSource interface {
   503→	// GetAdditionalSessions returns sessions not yet on entire/sessions branch.
   504→	GetAdditionalSessions() ([]*Session, error)
   505→}
   506→
   507→// OrphanedItemsLister is an optional interface for strategies that can identify
   508→// orphaned items (shadow branches, session states, checkpoints) that should be
   509→// cleaned up. This is used by the "entire session cleanup" command.
   510→//
   511→// ListAllCleanupItems() automatically discovers all registered strategies, checks
   512→// if they implement OrphanedItemsLister, and combines their orphaned items.
   513→type OrphanedItemsLister interface {
   514→	// ListOrphanedItems returns items created by this strategy that are now orphaned.
   515→	// Each strategy defines what "orphaned" means for its own data structures.
   516→	ListOrphanedItems() ([]CleanupItem, error)
   517→}

input.subject: Write tests for phase transition wiring in hook handlers
input.description:
Write unit tests that verify:
1. handleSessionStartCommon() calls Transition(phase, EventSessionStart) and dispatches actions
2. InitializeSession() calls Transition(phase, EventTurnStart) and sets phase on state
3. commitWithMetadata() (Stop handler) calls Transition(phase, EventTurnEnd) and triggers condense when ACTIVE_COMMITTED→IDLE
4. markSessionEnded() calls Transition(phase, EventSessionStop) and sets phase=ENDED
5. All hook handlers dispatch ActionUpdateLastInteraction

Tests should be written FIRST before implementation (TDD).

result.output: Task #1 created successfully: Write tests for phase transition wiring in hook handlers

input.subject: Wire Transition() into InitializeSession (EventTurnStart)
input.description:
Modify strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go InitializeSession() to:
- Call session.Transition(state.Phase, EventTurnStart, ctx) 
- Set state.Phase = result.NewPhase
- Dispatch ActionUpdateLastInteraction (update LastInteractionTime)
- Dispatch ActionClearEndedAt if present (clear EndedAt timestamp)

Key transitions:
- IDLE → ACTIVE (normal start)
- ENDED → ACTIVE (session re-entry, with ClearEndedAt)
- ACTIVE → ACTIVE (Ctrl-C recovery)
- ACTIVE_COMMITTED → ACTIVE (Ctrl-C recovery after commit)

result.output: Task #2 created successfully: Wire Transition() into InitializeSession (EventTurnStart)

input.subject: Wire Transition() into commitWithMetadata (EventTurnEnd/Stop)
input.description:
Modify cli/hooks_claudecode_handlers.go commitWithMetadata() to:
- After SaveChanges succeeds, call session.Transition(state.Phase, EventTurnEnd, ctx)
- Set state.Phase = result.NewPhase
- Dispatch ActionUpdateLastInteraction
- If ActionCondense is in result.Actions → trigger immediate condensation (was ACTIVE_COMMITTED)
- Save updated state

Key transitions:
- ACTIVE → IDLE (normal stop)
- ACTIVE_COMMITTED → IDLE + ActionCondense (condense at stop)

result.output: Task #3 created successfully: Wire Transition() into commitWithMetadata (EventTurnEnd/Stop)

input.subject: Wire Transition() into markSessionEnded (EventSessionStop)
input.description:
Modify cli/hooks_claudecode_handlers.go markSessionEnded() to:
- Call session.Transition(state.Phase, EventSessionStop, ctx)
- Set state.Phase = result.NewPhase (ENDED)
- Dispatch ActionUpdateLastInteraction
- Keep existing EndedAt timestamp setting

Key transitions:
- Any phase → ENDED

result.output: Task #4 created successfully: Wire Transition() into markSessionEnded (EventSessionStop)

input.subject: Wire Transition() into handleSessionStartCommon (EventSessionStart)
input.description:
Modify cli/hooks.go handleSessionStartCommon() to:
- Load session state for the current session
- Call session.Transition(state.Phase, EventSessionStart, ctx)
- Dispatch ActionClearEndedAt if present
- Dispatch ActionWarnStaleSession if present (for ACTIVE sessions from other agents)
- Save updated state if changed

Key transitions:
- ENDED → IDLE + ClearEndedAt (re-entry)
- IDLE → IDLE (no-op)
- ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED → same + WarnStaleSession

# Requesting Code Review

Dispatch superpowers:code-reviewer subagent to catch issues before they cascade.

**Core principle:** Review early, review often.

## When to Request Review

**Mandatory:**
- After each task in subagent-driven development
- After completing major feature
- Before merge to main

**Optional but valuable:**
- When stuck (fresh perspective)
- Before refactoring (baseline check)
- After fixing complex bug

## How to Request

**1. Get git SHAs:**
```bash
BASE_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1)  # or origin/main
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
```

**2. Dispatch code-reviewer subagent:**

Use Task tool with superpowers:code-reviewer type, fill template at `code-reviewer.md`

**Placeholders:**
- `{WHAT_WAS_IMPLEMENTED}` - What you just built
- `{PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS}` - What it should do
- `{BASE_SHA}` - Starting commit
- `{HEAD_SHA}` - Ending commit
- `{DESCRIPTION}` - Brief summary

**3. Act on feedback:**
- Fix Critical issues immediately
- Fix Important issues before proceeding
- Note Minor issues for later
- Push back if reviewer is wrong (with reasoning)

## Example

```
[Just completed Task 2: Add verification function]

You: Let me request code review before proceeding.

BASE_SHA=$(git log --oneline | grep "Task 1" | head -1 | awk '{print }')
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

[Dispatch superpowers:code-reviewer subagent]
  WHAT_WAS_IMPLEMENTED: Verification and repair functions for conversation index
  PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: Task 2 from docs/plans/deployment-plan.md
  BASE_SHA: a7981ec
  HEAD_SHA: 3df7661
  DESCRIPTION: Added verifyIndex() and repairIndex() with 4 issue types

[Subagent returns]:
  Strengths: Clean architecture, real tests
  Issues:
    Important: Missing progress indicators
    Minor: Magic number (100) for reporting interval
  Assessment: Ready to proceed

You: [Fix progress indicators]
[Continue to Task 3]
```

## Integration with Workflows

**Subagent-Driven Development:**
- Review after EACH task
- Catch issues before they compound
- Fix before moving to next task

**Executing Plans:**
- Review after each batch (3 tasks)
- Get feedback, apply, continue

**Ad-Hoc Development:**
- Review before merge
- Review when stuck

## Red Flags

**Never:**
- Skip review because "it's simple"
- Ignore Critical issues
- Proceed with unfixed Important issues
- Argue with valid technical feedback

**If reviewer wrong:**
- Push back with technical reasoning
- Show code/tests that prove it works
- Request clarification

See template at: requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md

Base directory for this skill: /Users/alex/.claude/skills/github-pr-review

# GitHub PR Review

## Overview

Technical mechanics for GitHub PR review workflows via `gh` CLI. Covers fetching review comments, replying to threads, creating/updating PRs.

**Companion skill:** For *how to evaluate* feedback, see `superpowers:receiving-code-review`. This skill covers *how to interact* with GitHub.

**Security:** Use fine-grained PAT with minimal permissions.

## Setup (One-Time)

### Fine-Grained PAT

Create at github.com -> Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens -> Fine-grained tokens:

| Permission | Level |
|------------|-------|
| Pull requests | Read & Write |
| Contents | Read |

**Can't:** Delete repos, push code, delete branches, manage settings.

### Configure & Allowlist

```bash
export GH_TOKEN="github_pat_xxxx"
```

Add to `.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": [
      "Bash(gh repo view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr view:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr create:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr ready:*)",
      "Bash(gh pr edit:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments:*)",
      "Bash(gh api repos/*/*/pulls/*/comments/*/replies:*)"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Quick Reference

| Operation | Command |
|-----------|---------|
| Get owner/repo | `gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"'` |
| Get PR number | `gh pr view --json number -q .number` |
| Get PR author | `gh pr view --json author -q .author.login` |
| Fetch all review comments | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments --paginate` |
| Get single comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/comments/{comment_id}` |
| Reply to comment | `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/comments/{comment_id}/replies -f body="msg"` |
| Create PR | `gh pr create --title "T" --body "B" [--draft]` |
| Mark ready | `gh pr ready [number]` |
| Convert to draft | `gh pr ready --undo [number]` |
| Edit PR | `gh pr edit [number] --title "T" --body "B"` |

## Workflow: Respond to PR Review

### 1. Get repo info and PR details

```bash
owner_repo=$(gh repo view --json owner,name -q '"\(.owner.login)/\(.name)"')
pr_number=$(gh pr view --json number -q .number)
pr_author=$(gh pr view --json author -q .author.login)
```

### 2. Fetch and analyze threads

```bash
# Fetch all comments and group into threads, showing last author per thread
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq 'sort_by([.in_reply_to_id // .id, .created_at]) | group_by(.in_reply_to_id // .id) | map({thread_id: (.[0].in_reply_to_id // .[0].id), path: .[0].path, line: (.[0].line // .[0].original_line), last_author: .[-1].user.login, last_body: .[-1].body[0:100], count: length})'
```

### 3. Filter to threads needing response

```bash
# Filter to threads where last_author != PR author
# Note: Use '| not' instead of '!=' to avoid shell escaping issues with !
... | jq --arg author "$pr_author" '[.[] | select(.last_author == $author | not)]'
```

For each thread needing response:
- Read the comment + file/line context
- Apply `superpowers:receiving-code-review` skill for evaluation
- Fix code and/or reply to thread

### 4. Commit fixes and push
- run the build, tests, linting as required
- commit the changes, noting the commit sha
- push the changes so they're visible
- We need to do this FIRST so we have the commit shas to put into the replies to the pr review

### 5. Re-fetch comment IDs (if rebased)

**Important:** If you rebased or force-pushed, comment IDs may have changed. Re-fetch the comment threads before replying:

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments --paginate | jq '...'
```

### 6. Reply to a thread

```bash
gh api repos/${owner_repo}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments/{comment_id}/replies \
  -f body="Fixed in commit abc123. [description of fix]"
```

### 7. Summarize and finish

After all threads addressed, ask if ready to mark PR ready for review.

**Note:** REST API doesn't expose "resolved" status. We infer "done" when PR author made last comment in thread.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| Broad PAT permissions | Use fine-grained PAT with only Pull requests + Contents |
| Missing pagination | Always use `--paginate` for comment fetching |
| Top-level reply | Use `/comments/{id}/replies` endpoint, not `/comments` |
| Re-responding to threads | Skip threads where PR author made last comment |
| Forgetting to reply after fix | Always reply to confirm the fix was made |
| jq `!=` fails with shell error | Use `select(.x == "y" \| not)` instead of `select(.x != "y")` |
| 404 on reply after rebase | Comment IDs change after force-push/rebase. Re-fetch comments before replying |

**Task 5: Phase-Aware PostCommit** — Wire `EventGitCommit` into `PostCommit()`. Instead of always condensing on commit, use the state machine to decide:
- ACTIVE + GitCommit → ACTIVE_COMMITTED (defer condensation, migrate shadow branch)
- IDLE + GitCommit → condense immediately
- ENDED + GitCommit → condense if files touched, discard if not
- Skip entirely during rebase (detect `.git/rebase-merge/` or `.git/rebase-apply/`)

# Executing Plans

## Overview

Load plan, review critically, execute tasks in batches, report for review between batches.

**Core principle:** Batch execution with checkpoints for architect review.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the executing-plans skill to implement this plan."

## The Process

### Step 1: Load and Review Plan
1. Read plan file
2. Review critically - identify any questions or concerns about the plan
3. If concerns: Raise them with your human partner before starting
4. If no concerns: Create TodoWrite and proceed

### Step 2: Execute Batch
**Default: First 3 tasks**

For each task:
1. Mark as in_progress
2. Follow each step exactly (plan has bite-sized steps)
3. Run verifications as specified
4. Mark as completed

### Step 3: Report
When batch complete:
- Show what was implemented
- Show verification output
- Say: "Ready for feedback."

### Step 4: Continue
Based on feedback:
- Apply changes if needed
- Execute next batch
- Repeat until complete

### Step 5: Complete Development

After all tasks complete and verified:
- Announce: "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch
- Follow that skill to verify tests, present options, execute choice

## When to Stop and Ask for Help

**STOP executing immediately when:**
- Hit a blocker mid-batch (missing dependency, test fails, instruction unclear)
- Plan has critical gaps preventing starting
- You don't understand an instruction
- Verification fails repeatedly

**Ask for clarification rather than guessing.**

    16→## Terminology
    17→
    18→- **Checkpoint** = data condensed to `entire/checkpoints/v1`, linked to a user commit
    19→  via `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. Permanent storage. Created at commit time.
    20→- **Step** = shadow branch commit, one per SaveChanges (each agent turn). Rewindable.
    21→  Ephemeral until condensed into a checkpoint.
    22→
    23→A checkpoint may contain multiple steps' worth of data. The shadow branch accumulates
    24→steps until the user commits, at which point they are condensed into a checkpoint.

    28→## Context
    29→
    30→When an AI agent commits via Bash mid-session (between UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks), `post-commit` fires and prematurely condenses session data, resets step count, and deletes the shadow branch. This causes:
    31→
    32→- **ENT-194**: Sequential agent commits produce empty/incomplete checkpoints because each `post-commit` condenses before the transcript is complete
    33→- **ENT-221**: No cross-hook state tracking means hooks can't distinguish "agent committed mid-session" from "user committed between sessions"
    34→
    35→The fix introduces a **session phase state machine** so hooks know the session's lifecycle stage.
    36→
    37→**Note:** File locking for concurrent hook access is deferred to ENT-238 (SQLite migration).
    38→The current atomic write-then-rename approach is retained, with a known narrow race window
    39→for concurrent hook processes.

    41→## State Machine
    42→
    43→### States
    44→
    45→| State | Description |
    46→|---|---|
    47→| **ACTIVE** | Agent is working on a turn. Set on UserPromptSubmit, cleared on Stop. |
    48→| **ACTIVE_COMMITTED** | Agent is working AND has made git commits this session. PostCommit defers condensation. |
    49→| **IDLE** | Turn finished, session still alive. Condensable on next user commit. |
    50→| **ENDED** | Session process exited. Condensable on next commit (if FilesTouched), otherwise discardable. |
    51→
    52→Note: UNINITIALIZED is not a stored state — it means no state file exists yet.
    53→Empty/missing Phase field in existing state files is treated as IDLE (backward compat).
    54→
    55→### Transitions
    56→
    57→```
    58→UNINITIALIZED ──UserPromptSubmit──────> ACTIVE           (state file created)
    59→ACTIVE ──Stop─────────────────────────> IDLE
    60→ACTIVE ──UserPromptSubmit─────────────> ACTIVE           (Ctrl-C recovery: just continue)
    61→ACTIVE ──git commit───────────────────> ACTIVE_COMMITTED
    62→ACTIVE ──SessionStop──────────────────> ENDED            (graceful shutdown, no turn completed)
    63→ACTIVE_COMMITTED ──git commit─────────> ACTIVE_COMMITTED
    64→ACTIVE_COMMITTED ──Stop───────────────> IDLE             ← triggers condense action
    65→ACTIVE_COMMITTED ──SessionStop────────> ENDED            (agent died after committing)
    66→IDLE ──git commit─────────────────────> IDLE             ← triggers condense action
    67→IDLE ──UserPromptSubmit───────────────> ACTIVE
    68→IDLE ──SessionStop────────────────────> ENDED
    69→ENDED ──SessionStart (re-entry)───────> IDLE             (clear EndedAt, immediately condensable)
    70→ENDED ──git commit────────────────────> ENDED            ← triggers condense/discard action
    71→IDLE/ENDED ──UserPromptSubmit─────────> ACTIVE           (clear EndedAt if needed)
    72→```
    73→
    74→Condensation is an **action** triggered by certain transitions, not a state. The state
    75→machine declares `ActionCondense` (or `ActionCondenseIfFilesTouched` / `ActionDiscardIfNoFiles`)
    76→in the transition result; the caller executes it. See the transition table in Task 1 for
    77→the full action mapping.
    78→
    79→**SessionStart re-entry:** When `SessionStart` fires and a state file exists:
    80→- Phase = ENDED → set Phase = IDLE, clear EndedAt (session re-entered, immediately condensable)
    81→- Phase = IDLE → no-op (already condensable)
    82→- Phase = ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED → leave as-is (warn user about stale session)
    83→- No state file → UNINITIALIZED (wait for UserPromptSubmit to create state)
    84→
    85→### Key Behaviors
    86→
    87→- **ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED**: `post-commit` defers condensation, only updates BaseCommit + migrates shadow branch
    88→- **ACTIVE_COMMITTED → IDLE**: Stop triggers immediate condensation (agent's commits already exist on branch)
    89→- **ACTIVE → ACTIVE (Ctrl-C recovery)**: Just reset to ACTIVE for new turn. No catch-up checkpoint. Interrupted turn's transcript data folds into next step naturally.
    90→- **ACTIVE/ACTIVE_COMMITTED → ENDED (SessionStop)**: Graceful shutdown without a completed turn. Shadow branch data preserved, condensable on next commit or via `entire sessions fix`.
    91→- **Shadow branch deletion**: Only when ALL sessions on the branch are condensed or discarded
    92→- **PendingCheckpointID**: Generated once per checkpoint cycle, shared across all commits in a session
    93→- **Rebase/merge detection**: PostCommit skips phase transitions during sequence operations (`.git/rebase-merge/` or `.git/rebase-apply/` present)
    94→
    95→### Condensation Eligibility
    96→
    97→| Phase | FilesTouched? | Action |
    98→|---|---|---|
    99→| ACTIVE / IDLE | Any | **Condense** (session ongoing, context valuable) |
   100→| ENDED | Non-empty | **Condense** (contributed to code) |
   101→| ENDED | Empty | **Discard** (no code contribution, noise) |
   102→
   103→**Simplified rule:** Discard only when `ENDED AND len(FilesTouched) == 0`.
   104→
   105→Additionally, users can explicitly remove a session from checkpointing via `entire reset --session <id>`. This clears the session state; any file changes remain in the working directory for the user to handle via git.
   106→
   107→### Stale Session Detection
   108→
   109→No automatic timeout detection. Instead:
   110→
   111→- **SessionStart warning**: If other sessions exist with no interaction in ~hours, show:
   112→  `"Found N session(s) with no recent activity. Run 'entire sessions fix' to resolve."`
   113→- **`entire sessions fix`**: User-initiated command. Scans for sessions in pathological states
   114→  (ACTIVE_COMMITTED with no running agent, old ENDED sessions). Shows session info (phase,
   115→  last seen, shadow branch data). Lets user choose per session: Condense / Discard / Skip.
   116→- **`entire status`**: Enhanced to show session phases and stuck states.
   117→
   118→**Rationale:** TTL-based detection causes false positives (long builds, permission prompts,
   119→complex reasoning). Users can determine session liveness better than any heuristic.
   120→
   121→### `LastInteractionTime`
   122→
   123→Updated on **every hook invocation** — UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, etc.
   124→Provides accurate "last seen" signal for the `entire sessions fix` UI and SessionStart warning.
   125→
   126→### Known Limitations
   127→
   128→**Ctrl-C interruption:** When a user Ctrl-C's during agent work, no hook fires. The session
   129→stays in ACTIVE. On next UserPromptSubmit → ACTIVE → ACTIVE transition → just continue.
   130→The interrupted turn gets no rewind point (step), but its transcript lines fold into the next
   131→step. Files modified during the interrupted turn are captured via `git status` in subsequent
   132→steps, though without fine-grained transcript attribution.
   133→
   134→**ACTIVE_COMMITTED + dead agent:** If an agent commits mid-session and then crashes (no Stop
   135→hook fires), the session is stuck in ACTIVE_COMMITTED. PostCommit will always defer for this
   136→session. Resolution: user runs `entire sessions fix` to condense or discard. Data is safe on
   137→the shadow branch until resolved.
   138→
   139→**Backward compatibility:** Existing sessions without a Phase field are treated as IDLE
   140→(empty → IDLE). In-flight sessions at code update time don't get the fix — they experience
   141→the same premature condensation bug that already exists. Only sessions started after the
   142→update benefit from phase tracking.

   201→    default:

   314→	// Get or generate checkpoint ID (ParseCheckpoint validates format, so found==true means valid)
   315→	if existingCpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(message); found {
   316→		// Trailer already exists (e.g., amend) - keep it
   317→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: trailer already exists",
   318→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   319→			slog.String("source", source),
   320→			slog.String("existing_checkpoint_id", existingCpID.String()),
   321→		)
   322→		return nil
   323→	}
   324→
   325→	if hasNewContent {
   326→		// New content: generate new checkpoint ID
   327→		cpID, err := id.Generate()
   328→		if err != nil {
   329→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to generate checkpoint ID: %w", err)
   330→		}
   331→		checkpointID = cpID
   332→	}
   333→	// Otherwise checkpointID is already set to LastCheckpointID from above
   334→
   335→	// Determine agent type and last prompt from session
   336→	agentType := DefaultAgentType // default for backward compatibility
   337→	var lastPrompt string
   338→	if hasNewContent && len(sessionsWithContent) > 0 {
   339→		session := sessionsWithContent[0]
   340→		if session.AgentType != "" {
   341→			agentType = session.AgentType
   342→		}
   343→		lastPrompt = s.getLastPrompt(repo, session)
   344→	} else if reusedSession != nil {
   345→		// Reusing checkpoint from existing session - get agent type and prompt from that session
   346→		if reusedSession.AgentType != "" {
   347→			agentType = reusedSession.AgentType
   348→		}
   349→		lastPrompt = s.getLastPrompt(repo, reusedSession)
   350→	}
   351→
   352→	// Prepare prompt for display: collapse newlines/whitespace, then truncate (rune-safe)
   353→	displayPrompt := stringutil.TruncateRunes(stringutil.CollapseWhitespace(lastPrompt), 80, "...")
   354→
   355→	// Add trailer differently based on commit source
   356→	if source == "message" {
   357→		// Using -m or -F: ask user interactively whether to add trailer
   358→		// (comments won't be stripped by git in this mode)
   359→
   360→		// Build context string for interactive prompt
   361→		var promptContext string
   362→		if displayPrompt != "" {
   363→			promptContext = "You have an active " + string(agentType) + " session.\nLast Prompt: " + displayPrompt
   364→		}
   365→
   366→		if !askConfirmTTY("Link this commit to "+string(agentType)+" session context?", promptContext, true) {
   367→			// User declined - don't add trailer
   368→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: user declined trailer",
   369→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   370→				slog.String("source", source),
   371→			)
   372→			return nil
   373→		}
   374→		message = addCheckpointTrailer(message, checkpointID)
   375→	} else {
   376→		// Normal editor flow: add trailer with explanatory comment (will be stripped by git)
   377→		message = addCheckpointTrailerWithComment(message, checkpointID, string(agentType), displayPrompt)
   378→	}
   379→
   380→	logging.Info(logCtx, "prepare-commit-msg: trailer added",
   381→		slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   382→		slog.String("source", source),
   383→		slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   384→		slog.Bool("has_new_content", hasNewContent),
   385→	)
   386→
   387→	// Write updated message back
   388→	if err := os.WriteFile(commitMsgFile, []byte(message), 0o600); err != nil {
   389→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   390→	}
   391→
   392→	return nil
   393→}

   395→// PostCommit is called by the git post-commit hook after a commit is created.
   396→// Checks if the commit has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer and if so, condenses
   397→// session data from shadow branches to entire/sessions.
   398→// If the user removed the trailer during commit message editing, this is treated
   399→// as a "manual" commit and no condensation happens.
   400→//
   401→//nolint:unparam // error return required by interface but hooks must return nil
   402→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) PostCommit() error {
   403→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   404→
   405→	repo, err := OpenRepository()
   406→	if err != nil {
   407→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   408→	}
   409→
   410→	// Get HEAD commit to check for trailer
   411→	head, err := repo.Head()
   412→	if err != nil {
   413→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   414→	}
   415→
   416→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   417→	if err != nil {
   418→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   419→	}
   420→
   421→	// Check if commit has checkpoint trailer (ParseCheckpoint validates format)
   422→	checkpointID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(commit.Message)
   423→	if !found {
   424→		// No trailer - user removed it, treat as manual commit
   425→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: no checkpoint trailer",
   426→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   427→		)
   428→		return nil
   429→	}
   430→
   431→	worktreePath, err := GetWorktreePath()
   432→	if err != nil {
   433→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Hook must be silent on failure
   434→	}
   435→
   436→	// Find all active sessions for this worktree
   437→	sessions, err := s.findSessionsForWorktree(worktreePath)
   438→	if err != nil || len(sessions) == 0 {
   439→		logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: no active sessions despite trailer",
   440→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   441→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   442→		)
   443→		return nil //nolint:nilerr // Intentional: hooks must be silent on failure
   444→	}
   445→
   446→	// Filter to sessions with new content
   447→	sessionsWithContent := s.filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo, sessions)
   448→	if len(sessionsWithContent) == 0 {
   449→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: no new content to condense",
   450→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   451→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", checkpointID.String()),
   452→			slog.Int("sessions_found", len(sessions)),
   453→		)
   454→		// Still update BaseCommit for all sessions in this worktree
   455→		// This prevents stale BaseCommit when commits happen without condensation
   456→		// (e.g., when reusing a previous checkpoint ID for split commits)
   457→		newHead := head.Hash().String()
   458→		for _, state := range sessions {
   459→			if state.BaseCommit != newHead {
   460→				state.BaseCommit = newHead
   461→				if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   462→					logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: failed to update session BaseCommit",
   463→						slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
   464→						slog.String("error", err.Error()),
   465→					)
   466→				}
   467→			}
   468→		}
   469→		return nil
   470→	}
   471→
   472→	// Track shadow branch names to clean up after successful condensation
   473→	shadowBranchesToDelete := make(map[string]struct{})
   474→
   475→	// Condense sessions that have new content
   476→	for _, state := range sessionsWithContent {
   477→		// Compute shadow branch name BEFORE condensation modifies state.BaseCommit
   478→		shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   479→
   480→		result, err := s.CondenseSession(repo, checkpointID, state)
   481→		if err != nil {
   482→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: condensation failed for session %s: %v\n",
   483→				state.SessionID, err)
   484→			continue
   485→		}
   486→
   487→		// Track this shadow branch for cleanup
   488→		shadowBranchesToDelete[shadowBranchName] = struct{}{}
   489→
   490→		// Update session state for the new base commit
   491→		// After condensation, the session continues from the NEW commit (HEAD), so we:
   492→		// 1. Update BaseCommit to new HEAD - session now tracks from new commit
   493→		// 2. Reset StepCount to 0 - no checkpoints exist on new shadow branch yet
   494→		// 3. Update CheckpointTranscriptStart - track transcript position for detecting new content
   495→		// 4. Clear PromptAttributions - they were already used in condensation, reset for next cycle
   496→		//
   497→		// This is critical: if we don't update BaseCommit, listAllSessionStates will try
   498→		// to find shadow branch for old commit (which gets deleted), and since StepCount > 0,
   499→		// it will clean up (delete) the session state file. By updating to new HEAD with
   500→		// StepCount = 0, the session is preserved even without a shadow branch.
   501→		state.BaseCommit = head.Hash().String()
   502→		state.StepCount = 0
   503→		state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = result.TotalTranscriptLines
   504→
   505→		// Clear attribution tracking - condensation already used these values
   506→		// If we don't clear them, they'll be double-counted in the next condensation
   507→		state.PromptAttributions = nil
   508→		state.PendingPromptAttribution = nil
   509→
   510→		// Save checkpoint ID so subsequent commits without new content can reuse it
   511→		state.LastCheckpointID = checkpointID
   512→
   513→		if err := s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   514→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: failed to update session state: %v\n", err)
   515→		}
   516→
   517→		shortID := state.SessionID
   518→		if len(shortID) > 8 {
   519→			shortID = shortID[:8]
   520→		}
   521→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Condensed session %s: %s (%d checkpoints)\n",
   522→			shortID, result.CheckpointID, result.CheckpointsCount)
   523→
   524→		// Log condensation
   525→		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   526→		logging.Info(logCtx, "session condensed",
   527→			slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   528→			slog.String("checkpoint_id", result.CheckpointID.String()),
   529→			slog.Int("checkpoints_condensed", result.CheckpointsCount),
   530→			slog.Int("transcript_lines", result.TotalTranscriptLines),
   531→		)
   532→	}
   533→
   534→	// Clean up shadow branches after successful condensation
   535→	// Data is now preserved on entire/sessions, so shadow branches are no longer needed
   536→	for shadowBranchName := range shadowBranchesToDelete {
   537→		if err := deleteShadowBranch(repo, shadowBranchName); err != nil {
   538→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Warning: failed to clean up %s: %v\n", shadowBranchName, err)
   539→		} else {
   540→			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Cleaned up shadow branch: %s\n", shadowBranchName)
   541→
   542→			// Log branch cleanup
   543→			logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "checkpoint")
   544→			logging.Info(logCtx, "shadow branch deleted",
   545→				slog.String("strategy", "manual-commit"),
   546→				slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName),
   547→			)
   548→		}
   549→	}
   550→
   551→	return nil
   552→}

   554→// filterSessionsWithNewContent returns sessions that have new transcript content
   555→// beyond what was already condensed.
   556→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) filterSessionsWithNewContent(repo *git.Repository, sessions []*SessionState) []*SessionState {
   557→	var result []*SessionState
   558→
   559→	for _, state := range sessions {
   560→		hasNew, err := s.sessionHasNewContent(repo, state)
   561→		if err != nil {
   562→			// On error, include the session (fail open for hooks)
   563→			result = append(result, state)
   564→			continue
   565→		}
   566→		if hasNew {
   567→			result = append(result, state)
   568→		}
   569→	}
   570→
   571→	return result
   572→}
   573→
   574→// sessionHasNewContent checks if a session has new transcript content
   575→// beyond what was already condensed.
   576→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) sessionHasNewContent(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) (bool, error) {
   577→	// Get shadow branch
   578→	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   579→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   580→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   581→	if err != nil {
   582→		// No shadow branch means no Stop has happened since the last condensation.
   583→		// However, the agent may have done work (including commits) without a Stop.
   584→		// Check the live transcript to detect this scenario.
   585→		return s.sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript(repo, state)
   586→	}
   587→
   588→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   589→	if err != nil {
   590→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit object: %w", err)
   591→	}
   592→
   593→	tree, err := commit.Tree()
   594→	if err != nil {
   595→		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit tree: %w", err)
   596→	}
   597→
   598→	// Look for transcript file
   599→	metadataDir := paths.EntireMetadataDir + "/" + state.SessionID
   600→	var transcriptLines int
   601→
   602→	if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileName); fileErr == nil {
   603→		if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   604→			transcriptLines = countTranscriptLines(content)
   605→		}
   606→	} else if file, fileErr := tree.File(metadataDir + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy); fileErr == nil {
   607→		if content, contentErr := file.Contents(); contentErr == nil {
   608→			transcriptLines = countTranscriptLines(content)
   609→		}
   610→	}
   611→
   612→	// Has new content if there are more lines than already condensed
   613→	return transcriptLines > state.CheckpointTranscriptStart, nil
   614→}
   615→
   616→// countTranscriptLines counts lines in a transcript, matching the counting method used
   617→// in extractSessionData for consistency. This trims trailing empty lines (from final \n
   618→// in JSONL) but includes empty lines in the middle of the file.
   619→func countTranscriptLines(content string) int {
   620→	lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
   621→	// Trim trailing empty lines (from final \n in JSONL)
   622→	for len(lines) > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(lines[len(lines)-1]) == "" {
   623→		lines = lines[:len(lines)-1]
   624→	}
   625→	return len(lines)
   626→}
   627→
   628→// sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript checks if a session has new content
   629→// by examining the live transcript file. This is used when no shadow branch exists
   630→// (i.e., no Stop has happened yet) but the agent may have done work.
   631→//
   632→// Returns true if:
   633→//  1. The transcript has grown since the last condensation, AND
   634→//  2. The new transcript portion contains file modifications, AND
   635→//  3. At least one modified file overlaps with the currently staged files
   636→//
   637→// The overlap check ensures we don't add checkpoint trailers to commits that are
   638→// unrelated to the agent's recent changes.
   639→//
   640→// This handles the scenario where the agent commits mid-session before Stop.
   641→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) sessionHasNewContentFromLiveTranscript(repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) (bool, error) {
   642→	// Need both transcript path and agent type to analyze
   643→	if state.TranscriptPath == "" || state.AgentType == "" {
   644→		return false, nil
   645→	}
   646→
   647→	// Get the agent for transcript analysis
   648→	ag, err := agent.GetByAgentType(state.AgentType)
   649→	if err != nil {
   650→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Unknown agent type, fail gracefully
   651→	}
   652→
   653→	// Cast to TranscriptAnalyzer
   654→	analyzer, ok := ag.(agent.TranscriptAnalyzer)
   655→	if !ok {
   656→		return false, nil // Agent doesn't support transcript analysis
   657→	}
   658→
   659→	// Get current transcript position
   660→	currentPos, err := analyzer.GetTranscriptPosition(state.TranscriptPath)
   661→	if err != nil {
   662→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Error reading transcript, fail gracefully
   663→	}
   664→
   665→	// Check if transcript has grown since last condensation
   666→	if currentPos <= state.CheckpointTranscriptStart {
   667→		return false, nil // No new content
   668→	}
   669→
   670→	// Transcript has grown - check if there are file modifications in the new portion
   671→	modifiedFiles, _, err := analyzer.ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(state.TranscriptPath, state.CheckpointTranscriptStart)
   672→	if err != nil {
   673→		return false, nil //nolint:nilerr // Error parsing transcript, fail gracefully
   674→	}
   675→
   676→	// No file modifications means no new content to checkpoint
   677→	if len(modifiedFiles) == 0 {
   678→		return false, nil
   679→	}
   680→
   681→	// Check if any modified files overlap with currently staged files
   682→	// This ensures we only add checkpoint trailers to commits that include
   683→	// files the agent actually modified
   684→	stagedFiles := getStagedFiles(repo) // TODO: does it work? Do we have staged files if this is called at post-commit hook ?
   685→	if !hasOverlappingFiles(stagedFiles, modifiedFiles) {
   686→		return false, nil // No overlap - staged files are unrelated to agent's work
   687→	}
   688→
   689→	return true, nil
   690→}
